name.en: Agigea bridges over the Danube–Black Sea Canal
name.ro: Podurile de la Agigea peste Canalul Dunăre–Marea Neagră

description.en: Two cable-stayed road bridges spanning the Danube–Black Sea Canal at its Agigea end, the road link between Constanța, its southern port and the seaside resorts. The 1983 bridge, designed by a team led by engineer Octavian Strâmbu, was the first cable-stayed bridge on a Romanian national road: 290 m long with a 162.5 m span over the navigable channel, high enough to clear canal shipping. A second, larger cable-stayed bridge 360 m long with a 200 m central span was built at km 0+540 and inaugurated on 19 October 2015 to relieve the original crossing.
description.ro: Două poduri rutiere hobanate peste Canalul Dunăre–Marea Neagră, la capătul dinspre Agigea, legătura rutieră dintre Constanța, portul de sud și stațiunile de pe litoral. Podul din 1983, proiectat de o echipă condusă de inginerul Octavian Strâmbu, a fost primul pod hobanat de pe un drum național din România: 290 m lungime, cu o deschidere de 162,5 m peste șenalul navigabil, la o înălțime care permite trecerea navelor. Un al doilea pod hobanat, mai mare, de 360 m lungime și cu o deschidere centrală de 200 m, a fost construit la km 0+540 și inaugurat pe 19 octombrie 2015, pentru a descongestiona traversarea inițială.

contract.noticeReference: 290 m long, of which a 246.65 m cable-stayed structure with a 162.5 m main span over the navigable channel; built from 1980 with floating cranes and self-compacting concrete, inaugurated 19 June 1983 as Romania's first cable-stayed bridge on a national road (OpenStreetMap records the opening as 1984)

Cable-stayed bridge 360 m long, 200 m central span, 17.4 m wide, at km 0+540 of the canal; the financing contract for the bridge and its access works to Constanța port was 191,797,112 lei. Inaugurated 19 October 2015 after a delay of nearly ten months, with press reporting that unrestricted traffic followed only later
